articles.title: Former officials urge Congress to reform permitting
articles.summary: Welcome to The Hill’s Business & Economy newsletter {beacon} Business & Economy Business & Economy The Big Story Former officials urge Congress to reform permitting A group of economic and national security officials across multiple presidential administrations are urging Congress to pass permitting reform legislation. © Greg Nash In a letter to Senate Majority Leader…
articles.body:
Former officials urge Congress to reform permitting

A group of economic and national security officials across multiple presidential administrations are urging Congress to pass permitting reform legislation .

In a letter to Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.), Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.), House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.), 19 officials from the Clinton, George W. Bush, Obama, first Trump and Biden administrations wrote that lawmakers have a “generational opportunity to strengthen” the country’s industrial capacity in the race against China.

“Critical industries across our economy — from semiconductors to critical minerals to artificial intelligence — are built in the physical world and powered by energy infrastructure that must be built as well,” the former government officials wrote. “Unfortunately, we are not building this infrastructure fast enough to remain globally competitive.”

Former Treasury secretaries Janet Yellen, Steven Mnuchin, Timothy Geithner, Henry Paulson Jr. and Robert Rubin, along with former Secretary of State Mike Pompeo, were among those who signed on to the letter. Seven former chairs of the Council of Economic Advisers also put their names down.

The officials lamented the time it takes to complete energy, industrial and infrastructure projects in the U.S., arguing the country is wasting its “advantages” in technology, capital markets, talent attraction, entrepreneurship and natural resources.

“Our inability to build threatens our national security and economic growth , and procedural barriers stymie efforts to correct course,” they wrote.

Two reasons why permitting delays “are especially concerning,” the officials argued, are the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence and rising demand for data centers.

Hyperscalers in the U.S. “have turned to on-site power generation solutions” to avoid permitting delays, with this “behind the meter” strategy resulting in higher costs for companies and the American public , the officials added.

“With a more rational permitting process, hyperscalers would invest in new energy infrastructure that could connect speedily to the grid, which, together with sound regulatory policies, would increase electricity supply for all consumers and ultimately reduce residential bills ,” they wrote.

Last month, Sens. Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.V.), Mike Lee (R-Utah), Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.) and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.) introduced legislation to reform the federal environmental review and permitting processes .

In their letter, the former government officials said the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act is the “most significant” permitting reform effort “in decades,” crediting the four senators for “taking bold action.”

They concluded, “If America can build at the speed our aspirations demand, it will be very hard for us to lose . If we cannot, it will be very hard for us to win.”

articles.title: Meta ordered to pay $25 billion in New Mexico case over Cambridge Analytica scandal
articles.summary: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion after the company was found to have misled users about its privacy practices in a case related to the Cambridge Analytica scandal.
articles.body: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion after the company was found to have misled users about its privacy practices in a case related to the Cambridge Analytica scandal. The Wednesday ruling marks one of the largest-ever legal penalties for a tech giant — and just the latest court loss for Meta this year. The company, then known as Facebook, disclosed in 2018 that the private information of as many as 87 million Facebook users was improperly obtained by political analytics firm Cambridge Analytica. The firm used that information to build profiles of American voters. New Mexico sued Facebook in 2021, accusing it of mishandling state residents’ personal information and deceiving those users about its policies in connection with the incident. A jury found in September that Meta had violated the state’s Unfair Practices Act more than 43 million times. State District Court Judge Francis Mathew criticized the company for what he described as a “coherent strategy designed to mislead the public” in his Wednesday penalty decision. “Facebook’s misrepresentations about users’ control of their data were not isolated incidents, but rather a systematic pattern of deception at the core of Facebook’s business model,” Mathew wrote. After Wednesday’s penalty decision, Meta said it will appeal the decision and has accused New Mexico’s attorney general of conflating privacy and speech issues. “This ruling, and the Attorney General’s approach to this enforcement, makes it all but impossible to do business in the state of New Mexico,” Meta Chief Legal Officer C.J. Mahoney said in a statement. “At its core, this lawsuit seeks to impose a tax on speech to enforce new rules for what people can say online. We are confident we will prevail on appeal.” Meta’s legal battles threaten to strain its business, though court penalties and settlements remain relatively small compared to the company’s earnings so far. The company reported earnings for the quarter ended in September on Wednesday, including lower quarterly profits than Wall Street had expected. It attributed the miss to a charge from the $18 billion multistate settlement it agreed to in August to resolve claims that its platforms have addicted and harmed young people. New Mexico was not a party to that settlement, which also resolved the participating states’ outstanding claims related to Cambridge Analytica. Meta posted income from operations of nearly $13 billion during the quarter, compared to nearly $23 billion that it said it would have earned without the settlement. Meta CFO Susan Li said on a call with analysts following the earnings report that the company is monitoring “active legal and regulatory matters that could significantly impact our business and financial results,” including additional youth-related trials set for later this year and next. Meta was also ordered to pay nearly $1 billion in a separate New Mexico case earlier this year over claims that its platforms addicted and harmed young people. Meta, along with YouTube, also lost a case in March in Los Angeles brought by a young woman with similar addiction and harm claims. The companies plan to appeal. Meta earnings Still, Meta’s business continues to grow at a strong clip thanks in large part to its investments in artificial intelligence. The company posted sales growth of 26% year-on-year to more than $64 billion in the quarter. Meta’s stock (META) jumped more than 3% in after-hours trading following the report on Wednesday. Meta launched its Muse AI personal assistant app in September. The app quickly rocketed to the top of app stores and has gained more than 10 million users, according to the company. It also launched its latest foundation model, Muse Wonder, last month. The company said Wednesday that its AI investments are boosting its core advertising business “through stronger engagement, better recommendations, and more efficient monetization.” Its average price per ad, a key metric for the company, jumped 14% year-over-year in the September quarter. Across the industry, tech companies face questions about their heavy spending on AI infrastructure. Meta’s capital expenditures during the quarter reached nearly $35 billion, up 80% from the year-ago quarter. And the company narrowed its full-year capital expenditure guidance to between $135 billion to $145 billion, the upper end of the range it had previously provided. Meta declined to provide spending guidance for next year. But investors are signaling they’re willing to give Meta some leeway, given the success of Muse, said Jesse Cohen, senior analyst at Investing.com. “The market has shifted from punishing Meta for spending to rewarding it for having a compelling product story,” Cohen wrote in emailed commentary.

articles.title: Stocks rise on AI-led earnings, France's 10-year bond yield hits 5%

articles.body:
By Caroline Valetkevitch and Dhara Ranasinghe

NEW YORK/LONDON, Oct 21 (Reuters) - Major stock indexes climbed on Wednesday, lifted by more strong results from AI-focused companies, while France's 10-year bond yield hit 5% for the first time since 2002 due to growing concern ‌about the country's economic outlook.

The Nasdaq gained more than 1%, with Super Micro shares rising 9.5% after the AI server maker ‌forecast quarterly revenue and profit margin above Wall Street estimates.

Shares of SpaceX shot up 7.8% after Elon Musk said late on Tuesday that a merger of his two companies SpaceX and ​Tesla would be "a good idea." SpaceX also posted its first profit as a public company.

AI-related shares sold off ahead of third-quarter results on investor worries about how long the AI trade can last.

"A lot of the concerns that we had over the last few weeks that sent the market lower are being alleviated," said Adam Sarhan, chief executive of 50 Park Investments in New York. Earnings "are coming in mixed to stronger than expected," which he called a relief.

"Tech ‌stocks fell hard last week on fears that the ⁠AI party is over," he said.

In addition, US bond yields have been falling after their recent run higher, and US interest rate hike expectations have waned, he said.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 360.21 points, or 0.69%, to ⁠close at 52,856.09, the S&P 500 rose 44.60 points, or 0.58%, to 7,757.17 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 278.04 points, or 1.05%, to 26,702.86.

After the closing bell, Meta Platforms shares gained after the Facebook owner raised the lower end of its annual spending forecast. Meta ended the regular session up 0.5%. Tesla shares also ​rose ​in after-hours trading as it reported a surprise positive cash flow for the third ​quarter. The stock ended the regular session up 3.4%.

MSCI's ‌gauge of stocks across the globe rose 7.48 points, or 0.7%, to 1,137.88. The pan-European STOXX 600 index climbed 0.92%.

US Treasury yields edged lower, with the yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note shedding 0.6 basis point to 5.111%.

Stocks have slipped of late and bonds have rallied due to concerns about the effect of higher borrowing costs on AI infrastructure stocks.

French bond yields rose again, with 10-year bond yields hitting a new 24-year high above 5%. The premium on French yields over benchmark 10-year German Bunds has also edged back toward early October's 15-year high of ‌nearly 160 bps.

French President Emmanuel Macron vowed to prevent a repeat of last weekend's ​violence at protests planned in the coming days, and dismissed as "stupid" and "unacceptable" comments from some ​foreign leaders about the unrest.

articles.body: Chennai: India’s carmakers are counting on Dhanteras and Diwali to sustain festive sales momentum, even as dealers’ body FADA reported a sharp year-on-year decline in passenger vehicle (PV) registrations during Navratri. The decline, however, needs to be seen against the high base created by the GST rate cuts in Sept 2025, which lowered vehicle prices and unleashed a surge in demand during the festive season.Maruti Suzuki, Hyundai Motor India and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles -- among the country’s top players, together accounting for two-thirds of PV sales -- have reported strong bookings and deliveries during Navratri, raising hopes that demand will hold up through Diwali.However, FADA reported a 22% year-on-year decline in PV retail sales during Navratri to 182,728 units from 234,004 units in 2025. Last year, buyers had deferred purchases ahead of the GST rate cuts that took effect on Sept 22, driving pent-up demand and inflating the base for this year’s comparison.Maruti Suzuki said retail sales between Ganesh Chaturthi and Dussehra rose 35% year-on-year, with small-car sales increasing around 16% and SUV sales doubling. Its retail sales during Navratri were almost on a par with last year. “The festive season has been encouraging for Maruti Suzuki, with strong customer demand through Navratri,” said Partho Banerjee, senior executive officer, marketing and sales of the company.Maruti began Oct with pending bookings of around 2 lakh units, which increased to 2.7 lakh after Dussehra. We expect double-digit growth over the overall festive period through Diwali, Banerjee said.Hyundai Motor India has also reported healthy demand, supported by sales during Onam and Ganesh Chaturthi. articles.title: Meta ordered to pay $25 billion penalty to New Mexico in data privacy case
articles.summary: Oct 21 (Reuters) - A judge in New Mexico ordered Meta Platforms on Wednesday to pay the state $25 billion after a jury found the company had misled consumers...
articles.body:
Oct 21 (Reuters) - A judge in New Mexico ordered Meta Platforms on Wednesday to pay the state $25 billion after a jury found the company had misled consumers about the privacy of their data, hitting the company with one of the largest financial penalties in US history.

The ruling came in a ‌case stemming from allegations that Cambridge Analytica, a British political consulting firm involved in Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign, obtained data from millions of Facebook users without their ‌consent. New Mexico had sued Meta, accusing it of lying to Facebook users in New Mexico about who had access to their data.

"Facebook's wrongdoing — over the course of years and systematically broadcast to the public — goes to the ​heart of Facebook's core business practices," Judge Francis Mathew wrote in his order, which came more than three weeks after the verdict.

Mathew found that a penalty of more than $219 billion was warranted based on state law, but he reduced the figure to $25 billion.

In a statement, C.J. Mahoney, Meta's chief legal officer, said the company is confident it will win on appeal.

"This ruling, and the Attorney General's approach to this enforcement, makes it all but impossible to do business in the state of New Mexico," Mahoney said. "At its core, this lawsuit seeks to impose a tax on speech to enforce new ‌rules for what people can say online."

New Mexico Attorney General Raúl ⁠Torrez said in a statement after the ruling the penalty was one of the largest financial penalties against a corporation in US history.

Meta previously faced a $5 billion penalty from the US Federal Trade Commission in 2019 over the Cambridge Analytica scandal.

Six other states settled their lawsuits against Meta related ⁠to Cambridge Analytica for $459.2 million as part of a $17.1 billion multistate settlement the company reached in August to resolve states' claims that the company's platforms had harmed teen mental health.

New Mexico's attorney general sued Meta in 2021 following revelations that Cambridge Analytica had harvested personal data from as many as 87 million Facebook users through a third-party app.

The state accused Meta of lying to Facebook users ​in ​New Mexico about who had access to their data and its handling of hate speech and misinformation posted ​on the platform. It alleged the company knew third parties had broad ‌access to users' data and tolerated hate speech or other harmful content when it benefited the company's bottom line.

articles.title: Tesla reports Q3 earnings beat, positive free cash flow, and better-than-expected capex
articles.summary: Tesla reported Q3 earnings after the bell.
articles.body:
Tesla ( TSLA ) reported better-than-expected third quarter earnings, with its free cash flow and capex spending coming in ahead of Wall Street estimates.

Tesla reported Q3 revenue of $28.05 billion vs. Bloomberg consensus of $28.13 billion. Tesla posted adjusted EPS of $0.48 vs. the $0.44 estimate, with adjusted EBITDA of $3.90 billion vs. $3.66 billion.

Tesla stock was volatile in after-hours trading.

Tesla reported free cash flow of $1.53 billion vs. an estimated -$4.92 billion, with capital expenditures climbing to $4.732 billion vs. an estimated $7.96 billion for the quarter.

On the earnings call, Tesla updated its full-year capex guidance to $20 billion from $25 billion previously. Tesla CFO Vaibhav Taneja said the savings would come from "managing our capital deployment efficiently, and plan to fund [capex] primarily from our cash flows from operations," he said.

"I think capex is actually ending up being a little lower than we anticipated, but we'll start to become more meaningful next year. And then noticeable in the tens of billions in '28," CEO Elon Musk said on the call.

The money is going to Optimus production lines, AI compute, the Cybercab ramp, and the Terafab chip plant Tesla is building with SpaceX.

Tesla revealed its Optimus robot started production at its Fremont factory. "While we will continue to iterate on the hardware and manufacturing process, we have proven that the current manufacturing process for Optimus is suitable for a commercial product," the company said in its earnings release.

"I would expect that it takes us probably at least a year — maybe a little longer — to get to that annualized rate [1 million units], to get to 20,000 units a week," Musk said on the earnings call. Musk added that Tesla may release an Optimus demo video in about a month, stressing that he didn't want the robot's movements to be preplanned.

Regarding its other AI efforts, Tesla said it plans to reach 400 MW of AI training compute by the end of the year. Tesla said its active FSD (full self-driving) subscriptions climbed to 1.74 million.

"The biggest driver of demand is full self-driving," Musk said regarding vehicle sales.

"The Cybercab fleet in Austin has grown by a factor of 10," Musk added while discussing Tesla's robotaxi fleet. He added, "I don't think there's any company in the world that can match our scale with autonomous vehicles."

Musk also stirred the pot recently with comments about a possible tie-up with SpaceX, his other company.

"I think both SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees to discuss this idea," Musk said during SpaceX's earnings call Tuesday night. "At the request of shareholders, and these special committees consist of independent directors. And because I'm a conflicted party, I can't actually be in the discussions of the special committees."

articles.body: MUMBAI: A surge in gold loans may partly reflect borrower stress, with lenders allowing customers already in deep delinquency to borrow against gold and repay overdue loans, Macquarie said in a report. Governor Sanjay Malhotra, deputy governor Poonam Gupta, executive director Indranil Bhattacharyya and external member Saugata Bhattacharya backed the shift. The duration and extent of any rate-hiking cycle would depend on underlying inflation, the spread of price pressures, second-round effects of supply shocks and demand conditions.“While inflation is driven largely by supply-side factors and does not show any signs of overheating of the economy nor of generalisation, it is important to manage inflationary expectations,” Kumar said. He favoured a 25-basis-point rate hike but said a neutral stance remained appropriate amid geopolitical and trade policy uncertainties.Singh warned that shifting to calibrated tightening could signal an extended rate-hiking cycle and undermine the benefits of recent growth-supportive monetary and fiscal policies.You use AI every day. articles.summary: BANGLURU/ NEW DELHI: Bengaluru-based digital trust and cybersecurity company eMudhra has acknowledged a cryptographic flaw that generated weak private
articles.body: BANGLURU/ NEW DELHI: Bengaluru-based digital trust and cybersecurity company eMudhra has acknowledged a cryptographic flaw that generated weak private keys linked to eight intermediate digital certificates in its global website-certificate business, potentially allowing attackers to impersonate legitimate websites. Shares fell 20% on BSE.The company said the affected TLS business accounts for around 1% of its revenue.eMudhra reported FY26 revenue of about Rs 710 crore and EBITDA of roughly Rs 110 crore. It had guided for revenue growth of 15–18%, with greater emphasis on higher-margin enterprise solutions.The flaw occurred during a key-generation ceremony on April 30, 2025, when a second set of weak keys was generated alongside the original strong keys. Mozilla cryptography engineer Dennis Jackson reported the issue on Oct 17, flagging insufficient randomness that made the keys vulnerable to recovery. eMudhra said it was investigating the root cause.eMudhra said it was working with affected customers to replace Transport Layer Security (TLS) certificates and prevent disruption. Co-founder Kaushik Srinivasan told TOI that no certificates had been issued from the affected root in India and that only one US customer had received certificates under the affected infrastructure. The company said its infrastructure had not been breached and its Indian digital signature certificate (DSC), eSign and enterprise solutions businesses remained unaffected.Govt officials said the ministry of electronics and IT has taken serious note of the incident with a special team constituted to investigate the matter.“The impact of this incident on Indian websites and applications have been very limited and for a very short interval… Important to note that Digital Signature Certificates and eSign services regulated by Controller of Certifying Authorities, remain completely unaffected by this incident,” an official said.Mozilla blocked six affected certificates, released Firefox security updates and removed the relevant root certificate from its trust store. Google blocked the affected public keys, extending protection to supported Android devices, while Cloudflare introduced safeguards. articles.title: Carmakers look to Diwali to rev up sales
articles.summary: CHENNAI: India’s carmakers are counting on Dhanteras and Diwali to sustain festive sales momentum, even as dealers’ body FADA reported a sharp
articles.body: CHENNAI: India’s carmakers are counting on Dhanteras and Diwali to sustain festive sales momentum, even as dealers’ body FADA reported a sharp year-on-year decline in passenger vehicle (PV) registrations during Navratri. The decline, however, needs to be seen against the high base created by the GST rate cuts in Sept 2025, which lowered vehicle prices and unleashed a surge in demand during the festive season.Maruti Suzuki, Hyundai Motor India and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles — among the country’s top players, together accounting for two-thirds of PV sales — have reported strong bookings and deliveries during Navratri, raising hopes that demand will hold up through Diwali.However, FADA reported a 22% year-on-year decline in PV retail sales during Navratri to 1,82,728 units from 2,34,004 units in 2025. Last year, buyers had deferred purchases ahead of the GST rate cuts that took effect on Sept 22, driving pent-up demand and inflating the base for this year’s comparison.Maruti Suzuki said retail sales between Ganesh Chaturthi and Dussehra rose 35% year-on-year, with small-car sales increasing around 16% and SUV sales doubling. Its retail sales during Navratri were almost on a par with last year. “The festive season has been encouraging for Maruti Suzuki, with strong customer demand through Navratri,” said Partho Banerjee, senior executive officer, marketing and sales of the company.Maruti began Oct with pending bookings of around 2 lakh units, which increased to 2.7 lakh after Dussehra. “We expect double-digit growth over the overall festive period through Diwali,” Banerjee said.Hyundai Motor India has also reported healthy demand, supported by sales during Onam and Ganesh Chaturthi. Registrations up to Navratri festival rose about 30% year-on-year to nearly 41,000 units.“Considering the pace of bookings, we expect momentum to continue through Dhanteras and Diwali. articles.title: With Trump polling at new lows, FCC chair issues warning about ‘fake polls’
articles.summary: With numerous reputable polls showing Democrats poised to make big gains in the midterm elections, the Republican chair of the FCC is advising local broadcasters to beware of “fake polls,” without specifying which ones he thinks are bogus.
articles.body: With numerous reputable polls showing Democrats poised to make big gains in the midterm elections, the Republican chair of the FCC is advising local broadcasters to beware of “fake polls,” without specifying which ones he thinks are bogus. Brendan Carr, a close ally of President Donald Trump, warned FCC-licensed stations on Wednesday, the same day two new, highly respected national polls showed Trump registering another record-low approval rating. His warning also came one day after a self-professed polling firm admitted to being a “fictional entity” that fabricated data and fooled news outlets. That’s a real — and infuriating — problem, but it shouldn’t besmirch the high-quality polls that are helping inform the electorate. So which polls was Carr warning about? His X post didn’t say, and he didn’t respond to CNN’s request for comment on Wednesday afternoon, leaving the matter nebulous. And perhaps that was partly the point. A group of former FCC officials called Carr’s message “part of an accelerating White House strategy to tilt the electoral playing field in the President’s favor and deny election results that don’t go his way.” The former officials also noted that “the FCC has zero authority to dictate editorial decisions.” Indeed, Congress has prohibited the FCC from trying to prevent the broadcast of any point of view. But the agency is responsible for licensing local radio and TV stations across the US and upholding basic standards, and Carr has repeatedly used that limited power to pressure broadcasters. Press advocacy groups argued that Carr’s latest post flew in the face of the First Amendment. “Literally every time he attacks the press, it’s because of reporting that was unfavorable to his boss, Donald Trump, whose gilded face he’s been known to wear as a lapel pin,” said Seth Stern, the chief of advocacy at the Freedom of the Press Foundation. Right now there’s a lot of unfavorable reporting about the Republican Party’s electoral prospects, given widespread voter dissatisfaction with the economy and the state of the country. Trump has defaulted to calling the polls “fake” and has occasionally threatened to match his words with actions. “I’ve been fighting pollsters,” Trump said at a rally on Tuesday. But if Trump has intended to chill reporting on public opinion, he hasn’t succeeded. Last month, an Iowa judge dismissed the president’s lawsuit against pollster J. Ann Selzer, her polling company, the Des Moines Register and Gannett. A spokesperson for Trump’s legal team vowed to appeal. On Wednesday, Carr claimed that this election season has brought “a significant surge in entirely Fake Polls and Suppression Polls designed to do nothing more than interfere with the regular functioning of the electoral process and alter the normal patterns of voter turnout and enthusiasm.” He said “many journalists and broadcasters have been amplifying or airing” the polls, though he didn’t name any polls or names. Carr then invoked the FCC’s power to penalize stations that violate the agency’s policies against “news distortion” and “hoaxes,” though those policies are narrowly tailored and rarely enforced. “Broadcasters are advised to avoid engaging in News Distortions or running Broadcast Hoaxes by airing Polls that would violate their regulatory obligations,” he wrote. Anna Gomez, the FCC’s lone Democratic commissioner, immediately spoke out against Carr’s message. “Pollsters who intentionally mislead the public should answer for it, but broadcasters who report publicly available polling data should never be punished when a poll is wrong,” Gomez wrote on X. “FCC rules on news distortion or hoaxes do not apply to a station that reports this data in good faith.” Stern made a similar point in a statement on Wednesday. “News broadcasters have a First Amendment right to report polling data, even if it proves to be inaccurate, just like they have a First Amendment right to report on Carr and Trump’s own countless lies and distortions, even when they turn out to be inaccurate,” he said. By inveighing against “fake polls,” Carr is once again embracing the rhetoric of the president who appointed him in 2017 and promoted him to chairman last year. The timing is striking, since the midterm elections are less than two weeks away and polls show Democrats with an edge in many key races. Many viewers and readers wonder about the reliability of polls, and the reality is that some are more trustworthy than others. Earlier this week, the poll-tracking site FiftyPlusOne prepared an investigation into a group called “Wedgewood Polls,” which had released more than a dozen election-season polls. FiftyPlusOne included the group’s data in its polling averages, but found evidence of fabrications. After the poll tracker asked for comment, Wedgewood issued a statement claiming it was an experiment “to demonstrate the vulnerabilities, lack of oversight, and overall low barrier to entry in the modern political polling industry.” FiftyPlusOne co-founder G. Elliott Morris charged that “they are trying to cover up their fraud with the ‘we were doing a social experiment’ excuse.” The American Association for Public Opinion Research condemned the fabrication on Wednesday. “Professional polling organizations are transparent, ethical, and work hard to provide critical information to the public and other stakeholders. It is important that we don’t conflate fraudulent activity like this with legitimate election polling,” the association’s president Mary Losch said. Even if it was just an experiment, it did real damage, playing right into the hands of public figures who want to sow distrust in even the most authoritative polling sources. “Fake news, fake polls, they’re all fake,” Trump said Tuesday. He then added in the next breath, “I have some great polls.”

articles.title: SBI confirms data leak, says 4,000 customer records identified on dark web
articles.summary: MUMBAI: SBI has confirmed a data breach involving 3,897 customer records containing personal information, which were found on the dark web.
articles.body: MUMBAI: SBI has confirmed a data breach involving 3,897 customer records containing personal information, which were found on the dark web.SBI identified the records containing personal information in a preliminary analysis of 3.75 lakh records found on the dark web.The bank said it had activated its cyber incident response protocols and commissioned an independent cybersecurity agency to investigate the incident after receiving alerts from its threat intelligence service provider, Defence Cyber Agency and CERT-In on Oct 16.The disclosure follows a claim by cybersecurity monitoring account CyberPulse that a threat actor using the name Siriusim had leaked documents and personal data allegedly linked to SBI. The post claimed the dataset contained 3,75,000 rows in CSV files and 2,722 PDF documents, including customer information, loan applications, supporting documents, account-opening forms and addresses.Independent assessment is under way: SBIThe authenticity and full extent of the alleged exposure had not been independently verified in the post.In its notice to stock exchanges, SBI said the preliminary analysis had identified records containing customers’ registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender, email addresses, residential addresses, branch and customer information file (CIF) identifiers, lead IDs and metadata associated with loan and lead records. The leak of PII can lead to impersonation, loan and benefit frauds and existing account takeovers.The bank said a detailed investigation was needed to establish the authenticity and completeness of the exposed data, determine its source and extent, and assess the risks to customers and the bank. It has engaged a cybersecurity agency empanelled by CERT-In, India’s national cyber incident response agency, to conduct an independent assessment. SBI said the incident had no material impact on its core business operations, financial performance or business continuity, adding that its core functions continued to operate normally. It said the assessment was underway and remedial and preventive measures were being implemented.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: HDFC Bank probes 2 executives for leak of sensitive information
articles.summary: MUMBAI: HDFC Bank is investigating whether two executives shared unpublished price sensitive information (UPSI) with outsiders in violation of Sebi
articles.body: MUMBAI: HDFC Bank is investigating whether two executives shared unpublished price sensitive information (UPSI) with outsiders in violation of Sebi regulations and the bank’s code of conduct. UPSI can include data on financial results, dividends, capital raising and the appointment of key managerial personnel. The probe comes as the bank prepares for a leadership change, with incoming MD & CEO Anup Bagchi set to take charge on Oct 27, a day after Sashidhar Jagdishan steps down.The bank confirmed that an internal probe was under way. “In line with our policies, a review is currently underway to gather and evaluate all relevant facts. To protect the integrity of the process and the privacy of all parties involved, we do not comment on active internal reviews,” the bank said.Info leak: HDFC execs may face regulatory actionEmployees can face regulatory action not only for sharing UPSI but also for trading in a company’s shares while in possession of such information. Sebi recently issued an administrative warning to Reliance Industries Ltd’ compliance officer after an investigation into trades between June and Aug 2024 found that two employees and an immediate relative had traded in the company’s shares while in possession of UPSI. The Securities Appellate Tribunal upheld Sebi’s insider trading penalties against a former employee of Nucleus Software who had shared advance information about the company’s “huge profits” with a relative.Bloomberg first reported the investigation into the alleged leaks. According to the report, the executives oversee key businesses and functions at HDFC Bank. The bank identified them during an internal investigation launched after some senior leaders grew concerned about possible information leaks, the report said, citing people familiar with the matter. The probe is continuing as the bank examines whether the information was misused, according to the report.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Brent crude tops $110 as fresh attacks in Saudi Arabia raise concerns over oil supplies
articles.summary: Oil prices edged higher on Thursday, with Brent crude trading above $110 a barrel.
articles.body: Oil prices edged higher on Thursday, with Brent crude trading above $110 a barrel. The rise came after fresh Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia prompted US to order some diplomats and their family members to leave American missions in the Kingdom.At the same time, concerns over shipping safety and oil supplies in the region also persisted.WTI crude was trading at $98.05, up 90 cents or 0.93%, while Brent crude stood at $110, up $1.15 or 1.06%.US officials told Reuters that the state department also plans to withdraw family members from several other American missions in the region.The latest security concerns followed a series of attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis on Wednesday. At least one person was killed and eight others wounded in an attack on a civilian airport in Dammam. A drone attack on a Saudi oil field killed two people.Explosions were also reported in Sirik, in southern Iran, on Wednesday. Iranian media said that the nature and origin of the blasts were unknown.Shipping risks extend beyond Strait of HormuzThe threat to energy supplies has extended to maritime routes beyond the Strait of Hormuz. Kpler data showed at least 18 attacks on shipping over the past two weeks.LSEG analysts warned that Iran was targeting tankers further afield, including in the Gulf of Oman. Such attacks were jeopardising Gulf crude loadings and ship-to-ship transfers that support regional loadings.Iran's leadership also issued fresh statements amid the tensions. Foreign minister Abbas Araqchi told the Financial Times on Wednesday that Iran was fully prepared to defend itself. President Masoud Pezeshkian told state media that the US could not expect dialogue while blockading and threatening Iran.US crude inventories fall, distillate stocks riseUS crude inventories declined by 3.06 million barrels last week to 412.5 million barrels, according to data released by the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) on Wednesday. The fall was greater than the 820,000-barrel draw expected by analysts in a Reuters poll.Distillate inventories, which include diesel and heating oil, increased by 1.68 million barrels to 104.3 million barrels during the week. Analysts had expected these stockpiles to fall by 1.16 million barrels, EIA data showed.Separately, the Trump administration is offering to loan up to nearly a third of the US emergency heating oil reserve, which holds one million barrels. The department of energy announced the move on Wednesday as the administration seeks to contain prices that have risen amid diesel shortages linked to the wars in Iran and Ukraine.Elsewhere, Russian President Vladimir Putin met US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg on Wednesday to discuss ending the war in Ukraine. The meeting came as Washington renewed efforts to end Europe's bloodiest conflict since World War Two.The Kremlin said Putin had agreed to resume US-mediated peace talks with Ukraine as soon as next month. articles.title: Wife’s father paid to buy house in couple’s joint names; Kerala High Court grants her exclusive ownership, rules husband must vacate after he fails to prove he paid anything
articles.summary: A property is in the joint name of a husband and wife. But only one of the two has directly or indirectly supplied funds for its purchase?
articles.body: A property is in the joint name of a husband and wife. But only one of the two has directly or indirectly supplied funds for its purchase? In case of a marital discord, who can claim ownership of it?The Kerala High Court has declared a house registered in a husband and wife’s joint names to be the wife’s exclusive property after finding that her father had funded the entire purchase. The court directed the husband to vacate the property within three months.The dispute involved a couple who got married in 2012. The woman maintained that her father had financially supported the couple and bought a house in the names of both his daughter and son-in-law.After the wedding, the woman accompanied her husband abroad, where they lived for some time before eventually returning to India.As the relationship between the couple deteriorated, the woman sought the return of her gold ornaments and asserted that the house belonged solely to her because her father had financed its purchase.Also Read | Homebuyers paid Rs 2.06 crore but got no flat, builder said payments meant accepting delay; Bombay HC orders interest payout from 2017 saying RERA allows for unconditional right to monthly interestWhat the case is aboutThe married couple’s dispute was related to a seven-cent plot with a residential building in Manjeri, Malappuram district. The property was purchased in 2015, and registered in both their names.The woman told the court that her father had paid Rs 30 lakh to purchase the house for her future security. Although the property was registered jointly, she maintained that her husband had contributed nothing towards the purchase and therefore had no independent entitlement to half of it.The Malappuram Family Court examined the evidence and accepted that the woman’s father had funded the purchase. However, it did not grant her exclusive ownership. Instead, it directed her husband to pay her Rs 15 lakh, which is the value of his half share.The husband challenged the decision, maintaining that he had bought the property using his own money. The woman also appealed, seeking a declaration of her exclusive ownership and an order requiring him to vacate the house.Also Read | Man sold his house and bought a Rs 1.10 crore flat jointly with wife; income tax department denies Rs 55.48 lakh capital gains exemption for half the amount, but ITAT Mumbai gives full reliefWhy did the court rule in the wife's favour?The woman’s father testified that he had raised funds through a loan. His bank statement showed a credit of Rs 25 lakh followed by a debit of the same amount on November 9, the date of the sale deed.The husband maintained that he had used his own money to purchase the property. However, he failed to present evidence explaining where the funds for the sale consideration had come from.When questioned on this during cross-examination, the husband acknowledged that he had not withdrawn the money from any bank account. Instead, he claimed that his brother-in-law, who was working abroad with him, had given him the funds.But the court noted tht he did not examine his brother-in-law or produce documents. The court noted that he had failed to establish that he paid any part of the consideration.It concluded that “the entire sale consideration was paid by the father of the petitioner.”Also Read | Man invested Rs 10 lakh, which tax department treated as unexplained; he first cited cash loan, then bank withdrawals as source, ITAT Nagpur deletes addition and Rs 2.11 lakh penaltyThe court also considered Section 45 of the Transfer of Property Act, which deals with the respective interests of people in property purchased using their separate funds. It found that the money had been provided by the woman’s father for her benefit and that the husband had not established a contribution of his own.It held that the appropriate relief was “declaring the exclusive ownership of the property upon the petitioner, while incidentally permitting her to obtain vacant possession thereof.”Asha Kiran Sharma, Partner at King Stubb and Kasiva, told ET that the Kerala High Court focused on who had actually financed the purchase rather than relying solely on the names recorded on the property's title deed.In this case, the wife's father established that he had paid for the house using funds raised through a bank loan.Sharma explained that Section 45 of the Transfer of Property Act provides that, when two or more people jointly purchase a property and there is no agreement to the contrary, their respective shares are generally determined by the amounts they contributed towards the purchase.Since the husband had not contributed any money, his name on the deed did not establish an actual financial interest in the property. The Kerala High Court therefore recognised the wife as the sole owner and directed her husband to vacate the house within three months.In effect, the wife's claim succeeded because her father's bank records provided evidence of the source of the purchase money.Sharma said that when parents provide money towards a property, the arrangement should be documented clearly as either a gift or a loan. Where co-owners contribute different amounts, the ownership proportions should also be specified in the title deed or a separate written declaration. This can help avoid disputes that may arise when a property is registered jointly but the financial arrangement rests on an informal, undocumented understanding.Also Read | Tenant claimed landlords withheld Rs 10 lakh security deposit and refused to vacate shop; Delhi High Court rules against him, orders payout for unauthorised stayYou use AI every day.
